title: The Society Book
logline: A village savings and funeral-aid society, run from a handwritten ledger, decides together how to help a member through a bad year, and turns down the easier option of interest that would eventually take the family's land.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: What is rigid made useful moves from a hide to a village: a mutual-aid society deciding how to help one member through a bad year rather than profit from it.

thread_out.thread: From a community holding one member in mind to a sculptor holding one face in mind, in detail, for weeks.

requirements: A long-running mutual-aid or funeral-aid society willing to be filmed
A real, current case, with full consent from the member involved
Trust and access built over enough time to observe genuine deliberation, not a performance for the camera

suggestions.name: A rural village with a long-running mutual-aid society
suggestions.why: Region-level suggestion for geographic variety; village mutual-aid and funeral societies of this kind are common across rural Sri Lanka.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts name lending to someone in trouble at unfair interest, so as to take their land later, as a wrong way to earn. A village that turns that easy option down together is doing something the texts count as good in its own right.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අමාරුවේ සිටින කෙනෙකුට අයුතු පොලියට ණය දී පසුව ඒ අයගේ ඉඩම අල්ලා ගැනීම වැරදි ජීවිකාවක් ලෙස දැක්වෙන බැවින්, ඒ පහසු මාර්ගය එකට ප්‍රතික්ෂේප කරන ගමක් කරන්නේ සැබෑ කුසලයකි.
lesson.the_teaching: Right livelihood, one of the three abstinences, exists when a person actually refrains from wrong conduct done to earn a living. The Pradeepika's own examples of wrong livelihood include lending money at unjust interest to someone in difficulty and later seizing their land, and putting others at risk for a small profit. The texts also teach that wholesome action has results of its own: resultant minds that carry the same names as the good acts behind them and arise from a person's own earlier actions, including during life as the enjoyment of pleasant things, with no judge handing them out.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The camera stays with the procedural texture: the monthly meeting, the handwritten ledger, the discussion of terms, and the care and discretion with which one member's situation is handled. The easier, profitable option is voiced and set aside, and the viewer sees the refusal as a choice made by many people together rather than a speech about virtue.

key_terms.en: right livelihood: refraining from wrong conduct done to earn a living

lesson.caution: This does not mean fair dealing is paid back quickly or that good people are always rewarded, and the texts' teaching on results must never be used to explain why any member is having a hard year.
lesson.builds_on: The drum-maker made something rigid usable; here a community's ledger and rules are turned toward helping one member rather than profiting from them, extending the market vendor's single refusal into a shared one.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
